newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean president's son to be summoned over Hanbo.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean president's son to be summoned over Hanbo.

text.p: South Korean prosecutors said on Tuesday they would summon President Kim Young-sam's son for questioning over controversial loans to the failed Hanbo Steel Co.
They said Kim Hyun-chul, the president's second son, earlier on Tuesday filed a complaint with them, saying that six opposition politicians had defamed him over the loan scandal.
"The prosecution will decide exactly when to summon Kim Hyun-chul after reviewing his complaint," a prosecution official told Reuters.

Hyun-chul said five members of parliament from the main opposition National Congress for New Politics and another party official had accused him of influence peddling in connection with the loans without any grounds. He has told reporters that he had nothing to do with the loans.
The five opposition lawmakers include National Congress spokesman Chung Dong-young, and his deputy Sul Hoon.
Hanbo Steel, flagship of South Korea's 14th largest conglomerate, was declared involvent on January 23 after racking up $5.8 billion in loans.
